episodes.173111: A slow-moving upper-level low pressure system with abundant moisture interacted with a backdoor cold front sliding southwest through eastern NM to produce widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms over NM during early October. Just enough instability and shear below the larger scale rotation aloft allowed a couple storms to produce brief funnel clouds over the region. A funnel cloud was observed near Edgewood.
episodes.174114: A weakening closed low moved across eastern Arizona and produced a few thunderstorms.
episodes.174518: Instability across the islands generated a couple rounds of showers, with brief periods of locally heavy rainfall, across portions of the Big Island and Maui. No injuries or damages were noted from this event.
episodes.174773: A shortwave trough approaching the area from the west along with moderate levels of instability (MLCAPE 1000 J/KG) and unseasonably high moisture content above the 90th percentile (PWAT 1-1.3) resulted in a favorable environment for the development of strong thunderstorms. A complex of strong thunderstorm activity developed north and west of Phoenix during the early to mid afternoon hours. This thunderstorm complex resulted in a strong outflow boundary, which surged southward across the Phoenix metro area between 1530MST and 1630MST. This strong outflow boundary produced areas of dense blowing dust as well as damaging winds, with widespread wind damage observed across several portions of the Phoenix area. Winds across the area remained elevated for approximately two hours, making the timing of the damages reported unclear. Other more isolated thunderstorm activity developed across the higher terrain east of Phoenix during the mid to late afternoon hours, with one  thunderstorm in particular affecting the Gold Canyon area, resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.174776: The combination of an approaching trough, increasing moisture from the Caribbean, a light southeast wind flow and local effects resulted in several active days across Puerto Rico. These factors enhanced the afternoon showers and thunderstorms for a few days. Additionally, the soils remained saturated from the rains in September, so several mudslides and flooding reports were received.

events.narrative: Hail of the size of nickels was reported along North 183rd Avenue in Surprise. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Social media video showed good flow along a wash that runs through the Gold Canyon Golf Resort, making several of the cart paths that runs through the wash impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
Emergency Managers reported that Quebrada Margarita was out of it banks, flooding several areas around San Patricio.
A post on social media indicated a large funnel cloud hovering over Twin Buttes Mesa near Navajo, NM.
Broadcast media reported that the police had to close Expreso Martinez Nadal due to significant flooding.
A social media user reported flooding along road PR-19, near Urb. Altamira. The road was impassable based on the shared pictures.
A funnel cloud was seen over Black Mesa from both Cow Springs and Tonalea.
A Forest Service employee spotted a funnel cloud near Edgewood around 445pm MDT on October 4, 2022.
